text: dsh-session-eval 是面向 DSH 的会话评估插件，通过 commands 和 sessionQuery 服务注册 /eval、/eval-diff 与 /eval-history。它从已保存的会话事件计算工具错误率、用户追问率和每轮工具调用量，并按固定阈值生成等级卡片；也能比较两个会话的变化、查看工作区最近会话趋势，或从导出的 ZIP 会话报告评分。适合回顾真实工作中的 agent 表现变化。需使用提供 commands 与 sessionQuery 的 DSH profile，不需要额外 API 密钥。

dsh-session-eval adds /eval, /eval-diff, and /eval-history to DSH. It scores saved sessions using tool-error, re-ask, and tool-load metrics, compares two sessions, summarizes recent workspace trends, and grades exported ZIP reports. Requires commands and sessionQuery services; no API key is needed.
想给刚结束的 DSH 会话生成表现评分卡。
我想比较改动提示词前后的两个会话有没有退步。
能不能按工作区查看最近几次 agent 会话的趋势？
希望把以前导出的会话 ZIP 也拿来评估。
I want a deterministic scorecard for a DSH session that has already ended.
How can I compare tool errors and usage between two sessions?
dsh-session-eval 的功能「会话评分卡」：/eval 默认评估当前会话，也可用 --id 指定会话或以 --report 读取导出 ZIP；输出可靠性、追问率和工具负载等级，可用 --json 获取结构化结果。
dsh-session-eval 的功能「会话差异比较」：使用 /eval-diff 指定前后两个会话 ID，插件比较工具错误率、追问率和工具负载，并以容忍微小波动的方式给出改善、退步或持平结论。
dsh-session-eval 的功能「历史趋势与报告」：/eval-history 可按工作区列出最近会话并比较首尾趋势；支持数量、--since 时间窗口以及 JSON 或文件报告输出。

**Retrospective evaluation for DeepSeek Harness agent sessions** — deterministic grade cards computed from sessions that already happened, plus cross-session regression diffs that answer *"did my agent get better or worse after that plugin / prompt / model change?"*
dsh-session-eval README · dsh-session-eval：No benchmark suites to author. No LLM judges. No new runs. Every grade is a fixed, documented threshold over persisted session logs — fully reproducible.

dsh-session-eval README · Install：**Requirements**: Node.js 20 or 22 · a DeepSeek Harness profile that mounts the `commands` and `sessionQuery` services (the shipped `web` / `agent` profiles qualify).

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-session-eval
```

Or from GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:kittimzhe/dsh-session-eval
```

The bundle overlay mounts `/eval`, `/eval-diff`, and `/eval-history`. If you maintain your own `cordis.patch.yml`, keep this row:

dsh-session-eval README · Install：```yaml
- insert:
    - id: session-eval
      name: 'dsh-session-eval'
```

dsh-session-eval README · Try it once：In DeepSeek Harness:

```text
/eval
```

Session eval — a1b2c3d4… (dsh-session-eval v0.2.2)
Overall: A
  Reliability   A    2/87 tool results errored (2.3%)
  Re-ask        A    1 re-ask signal(s) over 23 turns (0.4/10 turns)

dsh-session-eval README · Evidence-handoff closure (#8)：`/eval --report` grades straight from an artifact `dsh-session-export` already wrote — no session id to copy, and it works after the session is gone from the store:

```
recall "resume template font"
→ session session-ca62e005-… · report /proj/dsh-transcripts/bundle-ca62e005-20261104-120000.zip

/eval --report /proj/dsh-transcripts/bundle-ca62e005-20261104-120000.zip

dsh-session-eval README · Evidence-handoff closure (#8)：Bundle ZIPs (the nested `archive.zip` raw JSONL) and raw `/archive` ZIPs are both accepted. The JSONL inside is the canonical event log — the same bytes `readSession` returns — so `--report` grades **identically** to `/eval --id` (verified by a round-trip test against the real `dsh-session-export` writer). `--id` and `--report` are mutually exclusive.

dsh-session-eval README · Contributing：- **Local dev**: `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run bundle` (Node 20 or 22).
- **Start in the source**: [`src/grade.ts`](src/grade.ts) (thresholds, grade cards), [`src/metrics.ts`](src/metrics.ts) (metric extraction), [`src/trend.ts`](src/trend.ts) (`/eval-history` trend logic). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the source map and first-PR suggestions.
- **Open gaps**: [#1](https://github.com/kittimzhe/dsh-session-eval/issues/1) (configurable thresholds) and [#2](https://github.com/kittimzhe/dsh-session-eval/issues/2) (`/eval-history --since`) shipped in v0.3.0 — browse [issues labeled `good first issue`](https://github.com/kittimzhe/dsh-session-eval/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22).
- **Rules**: behavior changes need tests; doc changes must update `README.md` and `README.zh.md` in sync; version releases belong to the maintainer. Details: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

dsh-session-eval README · How it differs from benchmark-style evaluation：| | `dsh-eval` (benchmark) | `dsh-session-eval` (this) |
|---|---|---|
| Evaluates | Runs you launch ahead of time | Sessions that already happened |
| Setup | Author benchmark YAML + cases | None — read existing logs |
| Judge | Metric folding over trials | Fixed thresholds, deterministic |
| Best at | Pre-deploy benchmarks | Regression tracking over real work |

Both are useful; they don't compete. Benchmarks test what you *predicted*; retrospective evaluation watches what *actually happened*.

text:
dsh-session-eval README · Commands：| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/eval` | Grade card for the current session |
| `/eval --id <sessionId>` | Grade a specific session |
| `/eval --report <bundle-or-archive.zip>` | Grade from an exported artifact (works after the session is gone from the store) |
| `/eval --json` | Machine-readable metrics + card |
| `/eval-diff <beforeId> <afterId>` | Regression comparison, noise-tolerant |
| `/eval-diff … --json` | Machine-readable trend report |
| `/eval-history [N]` | Grade the last N sessions in this workspace and show the trend |
| `/eval-history … --json` | Machine-readable history report |
| `/eval-history --since 7d` | Grade only sessions with activity inside the window (`24h`, `30d` also parse) |

dsh-session-eval README · Commands：`--since` filters by each session's **latest activity**, not its creation time: a session opened long ago but active an hour ago stays in the window; a freshly created but silent one drops out. With `--since 7d` the trend compares the first and last of the in-window set, and an empty window prints a clear message instead of a crash. Without the flag, behavior is exactly as before (last N sessions).

dsh-session-eval README · Commands：Use `/eval-history --out report.md` to save the terminal card as Markdown, or add `--json` to save the JSON payload. Relative paths resolve against the current session workspace (the process working directory when unavailable). Parent directories must already exist; file errors are reported without creating directories. Existing output files are overwritten.

dsh-session-eval README · Commands：`/eval-history` finds the sessions for you via the same `sessionQuery` seam `/archive` uses (scoped to the current workspace's `cwd`), grades each, and diffs the first against the last. `/eval-diff` remains the tool when you already know the two ids that matter.

dsh-session-eval README · Configuring grade bands：The thresholds are defaults, not laws. A `gradeBands` block under the plugin's config node (naturally per-profile) overrides any dimension — values are the A–D upper bounds, ascending:

```yaml
session-eval:
  gradeBands:
    reliability: [4, 8, 15, 30]   # tool error-rate percent
    reask: [0, 2, 4, 8]           # corrections per 10 user turns

dsh-session-eval README · Configuring grade bands：Any subset may be overridden; unlisted dimensions keep the documented defaults. Unknown keys, wrong arity, non-numeric, negative, or non-ascending values fail fast at plugin load with a readable error — sessions are never graded against bands nobody chose.

Typical use: grade the ten sessions before and after a plugin or prompt change; a persistent `Reliability` regression is an early warning that the change hurt real work, not just benchmarks.

dsh-session-eval README · Dimensions & thresholds：All grades derive from three deterministic metrics. `n/a` when the session lacks the relevant activity.

| Dimension | Metric | A | B | C | D | E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reliability | tool error rate | ≤5% | ≤10% | ≤20% | ≤35% | >35% |
| Re-ask | corrections per 10 turns¹ | 0 | <1 | <2 | <4 | ≥4 |
| Tool load | tool calls per turn | 0.5–8 | 0.1–0.5 or just above 8 | <0.1 or 8–20 | >20 | — |

dsh-session-eval README · Dimensions & thresholds：¹ A *correction signal* is each extra user message inside a consecutive-user run — the human re-asking before any assistant reply, a behavioral proxy for "the agent didn't get it right the first time."

`Overall` is the **worst** graded dimension — conservative by design. Thresholds are constants in [`src/grade.ts`](src/grade.ts); making them configurable is on the roadmap (see issues).
dsh-session-eval README · Dimensions & thresholds：Diff verdicts include a noise band (±2pp error rate, ±0.5 re-ask, ±1 tool load) so trivial jitter doesn't cry regression.

dsh-session-eval README · Determinism guarantee：Same session logs in → same grade card out, every time, forever. There is no model in the loop, no sampling, no clock dependence in the metrics (wall time is reported, never graded). This is what makes `/eval-diff` trustworthy as a regression signal.
